name: text-to-event
title: TextToEvent
description: A pasted or selected message becomes a calendar event: title, date, time, place and people fill in one by one with per-field confidence, stay editable, then go to the calendar.

files.content:
/** Short, task-shaped instructions: the model copies what the message says; dates and times are resolved on device afterwards. */
export function eventInstructions(extra?: string): string {
  return [
    'Find the one event in the message. Return JSON only with these fields:',
    'title (a short name for the event, like "Dinner with Sara"),',
    'date (the day exactly as written, like "next Friday", "12 Nov" or "tomorrow"; optional),',
    'time (the start time exactly as written, like "8pm"; optional),',
    'place (where it happens, as written; optional),',
    'people (names of the other people, not "me" or "you"; optional).',
    'Copy words from the message. Leave out anything it does not say. Never guess.',
    extra,
  ]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(' ')
}

export { TextToEvent, textToEventLabels, type EventAddProps, type EventRowProps, type TextToEventIcons, type TextToEventLabels, type TextToEventProps, type TextToEventStyles } from './text-to-event'
export { useTextToEvent, refineEvent, toCalendarEvent, eventSchema, eventFieldNames, isoDay, toLocalDate, type CalendarEvent, type EventDraft, type EventFieldInfo, type EventFieldName, type RawEvent, type RefineEventOptions, type TextToEventState, type UseTextToEventOptions } from './use-text-to-event'
export { eventInstructions } from './prompts'

docs: Pass `onAdd` and write the event with expo-calendar (or your API). An unclear date ("next Friday" said on a Monday, "Thursday or Friday", 05/06) is highlighted with the days it could mean, and the add key waits until one is chosen.

budget.strategy: One structured call on the message; the model copies words, then dates, times and names are resolved and checked against the message on device.
